comments.value: Low dose (0.04 Gy) irradiation (LDR) and hindlimb unloading (HLU) microgravity in mice

studies.description: The purpose of the present study was to evaluate damage in brain and eye in a ground-based model for spaceflight which includes prolonged unloading and low-dose radiation. Low-dose/Low-dose-rate (LDR) gamma-radiation using 57Co plates (0.04 Gy) was delivered whole-body to mature, 6-month old female C57BL/6 mice to simulate the radiation component. Anti-orthostatic tail suspension was used to model the unloading, fluid shift, and physiological stress aspects of the microgravity component. Mice were hindlimb suspended and/or irradiated for 21 days. Tissues were collected at 7 days, 1, 4 and 9 months following simulated microgravity. Herein we proposed to use omics-based molecular phenotyping approach for identification and characterization of genomic signatures in multiple organ system associated with low-dose radiation and simulated microgravity.

protocols.description: Low-dose/Low-dose-rate (LDR) radiation using 57Co plates was delivered whole-body to mature, 6-month old female C57BL/6 mice to simulate the radiation component. A total dose of 0.04 Gy was delivered at a rate of 0.01 cGy/h over a period of 21 days; uniformity of dose was at ±5%. Mice receiving 0 Gy were handled similarly. Anti-orthostatic tail suspension was used to model the unloading, fluid shift, and physiological stress aspects of the microgravity component. Mice were hindlimb suspended and/or irradiated for 21 days. For combination group, mice were irradiated during tail suspension. Tissues were collected at 7 days, 1, 4, and 9 months following simulated microgravity. Cobalt-57 produces photons at three energies: 0.122 MeV (86%), 0.136 MeV (11%), 0.014 MeV (9%). Ionizing radiation energy values were added by GeneLab.
protocols.name: irradiation protocol

protocols.description: Brain samples were preserved in LN2 following isolation.
protocols.name: sample collection

protocols.description: Nuclueic acid extractions for RNAseq and RRBS: AllPrep DNA/RNA/miRNA Universal Kit (Qiagen, #80224) was used to perform RNA and DNA extractions. Frozen brain tissues were homogenized in 600 ul of RLT lysis buffer containing 1 % B-mercaptoethanol. Tissue homogenization was performed using tissue homogenizing bead mix (Tissue homogenizing CKMix, Precellys) on Minilys (Bertin Technologies). Tubes were centrifuged for 1 min at 20,000 x g to reduce bubbles/foam. The homogenized lysate was transferred to an AllPrep DNA Mini spin column placed in a 2 ml collection tube and centrifuged for 30 s at full speed (maximum speed of 20,000 x g). The flow-through (containing the RNA) was transferred into a new 2 ml microcentrifuge for RNA purification. 80 ul Proteinase K was added to the flow-through (RNA) and mixed by pipetting. 350 ul of 100 % Ethanol was added and mixed and incubated for 10 minutes at room temperature. 750 ul 100% ethanol was then added, mixed and transferred to an RNeasy Mini spin column placed in a 2 ml collection tube and centrifuged for 15 s at 20,000 x g. This step was repeated until the entire sample passed through the column. The flow-through was discarded. 500 ul of Buffer RPE was added to the RNeasy Mini spin column, centrifuged for 15 s at full speed (20,000 x g) and the flow-through discarded.10 ul DNase I stock solution was diluted in 70 ul Buffer RDD mixed gently and the 80 ul incubation mix was added to the spin column and kept for 15 minutes at room temperature. 500 ul Buffer FRN was then added to the RNeasy Mini spin column and centrifuged for 15 s at 20,000 x g. The flow-through (containing small RNAs) was re-applied to the spin column and centrifuged. The flow-through was then discarded. 500 ul Buffer RPE was then added to the RNeasy Mini spin column and centrifuged for 15 s at 20,000 x g. 500 ul of 100 % ethanol was added to the RNeasy Mini spin column and centrifuged for 2 min at 20,000 x g. The flow-through and the collection tube were discarded. Centrifugation was repeated with new collection tubes. The RNeasy Mini spin column was placed in a new 1.5 ml collection tube and 30 ul (for retina) or 60 ul (for brain) of RNase-free water was added directly to the spin column membrane and centrifuged for 1 min at 10000 x g to elute the RNA. The eluate was re-applied to the column and centrifuged again to increase the RNA yield from the column. RNA concentration was measured using Qubit 3.0 Fluorometer (Thermo Fisher Scientific). RNA samples were stored at -80 C until library construction.  The AllPrep DNA Mini spin column (containing the DNA) was processed for DNA purification according to the manufacturer's instructions. Briefly, 350 ul Buffer AW1 was added to the AllPrep DNA Mini spin column and centrifuged for 15 s at 20,000 x g to wash the spin column membrane. The flow-through was discarded. 20 ul Proteinase K was added to 60 ul Buffer AW1, mix gently, applied to the AllPrep DNA Mini spin column membrane and incubated for 5 minutes at room temperature. 350 ul Buffer AW1 was then added to the AllPrep DNA Mini spin column and centrifuged for 15 s at 20,000 x g and flow-through was discarded. 500 ul Buffer AW2 was then added to the AllPrep DNA Mini spin column and centrifuged for 2 min at full speed to wash the spin column membrane and the flow-through was discarded. The AllPrep DNA Mini spin column was placed in a new 1.5 ml collection tube and 30 ul (for retina) or 60 ul (for brain) of buffer EB was added directly to the spin column membrane and centrifuged for 1 min at 10000 x g to elute the DNA. The eluate was re-applied to the column and centrifuged again to increase the DNA yield from the column. DNA concentration was measured using Qubit 3.0 Fluorometer (Thermo Fisher Scientific). DNA samples were stored at -80 C until library construction.  RNA extraction for microarray: Total RNA of each tissue was extracted with the Qiagen RNeasy Mini Kit (Qiagen, #74104) according to specifications. RNA integrity and concentration were checked by Agilent NanoRNA Chip (Bio-Analyser, Agilent Technologies, Palo Alto, CA, USA). A minimum RNA Integrity Number of 7.6 was required for all samples.
protocols.name: nucleic acid extraction

protocols.description: For RNA-Seq library construction, 100 ng of total RNA was used as input spiked with 1 ul (%) of 1:500 diluted ERCC ExFold Spike-In Mix 1 (Ambion/ThermoFisher Scientific, cat 4455861) with resulting total volume of 5 ul.
protocols.name: spike-in protocol

protocols.description: The Ovation Mouse RNA-Seq System 1-96 (NuGEN Technologies, #9136-A01) was used per manufacturer's instructions to construct RNA-Seq libraries. 100 ng of total RNA was used as input. First and second strands of cDNA were synthesized from total RNA spiked with 1 ul of 1:500 diluted ERCC ExFold RNA Spike-In Mix 1 (Life Technologies) at the appropriate ratio. Following primer annealing and cDNA synthesis, the products were sheared using Covaris S220 Focused-ultrasonicator (Covaris Inc.). 130 ul of each sample was sheared according to manufacturer's instruction. The parameters were set as follows: 10% duty factor, peak power 175 and 200 cycles per burst at 4 C for 200 seconds to obtain fragment sizes between 150-200 bp. This was followed by end-repair, adaptor index ligation and strand selection. Barcodes with unique indices out of 96 indices, was used per sample for multiplexing. Strand selection was performed by using custom InDA-C primer mixture SS5 Version5 for mice. Finally, libraries were amplified using 17 cycles (Mastercycler pro, Eppendorf) and purified with RNAClean XP Agencourt beads.
protocols.name: RNA sequencing library construction

protocols.description: RNA sequencing was performed on Illumina HiSeq 4000 single read 75 bp.  DNA sequencing was performed on Illumina NextSeq 550 or HiSeq 4000 single read 70 bp. Several samples were re-sequenced to get enough reads and the CFG s were kept the same for the same sample across repeated sequence runs.
protocols.name: nucleic acid sequencing

protocols.description: Raw fastq files were assessed for % rRNA using HTStream SeqScreener (version 1.0.0) and filtered using Trim Galore! (version 0.6.10). Raw and trimmed fastq file quality was evaluated with FastQC (version 0.12.1), and MultiQC (version 1.26) was used to generate MultiQC reports.
protocols.name: GeneLab raw data processing protocol

protocols.description: Data were processed as described in GL-DPPD-7101-G (https://github.com/nasa/GeneLab_Data_Processing/blob/master/RNAseq/Pipeline_GL-DPPD-7101_Versions/GL-DPPD-7101-G.md), using NF_RCP version 2.1.0 (https://github.com/nasa/GeneLab_RNASeq_Workflow/tree/NF_RCP_2.1.0). In short, raw fastq files were filtered using Trim Galore! (version 0.6.10) powered by Cutadapt (version 4.2). Trimmed fastq file quality was evaluated with FastQC (version 0.12.1), and MultiQC (version 1.26) was used to generate MultiQC reports. Mus Musculus STAR and RSEM references were built using STAR (version 2.7.11b) and RSEM (version 1.3.3), respectively, Ensembl release 112, genome assembly GRCm39 (Mus_musculus.GRCm39.dna.primary_assembly.fa) concatenated with ERCC92.fa from ThermoFisher (https://assets.thermofisher.com/TFS-Assets/LSG/manuals/ERCC92.zip), and the following gtf annotation file: Mus_musculus.GRCm39.112.gtf concatenated with the ERCC92.gtf file from ThermoFisher (https://assets.thermofisher.com/TFS-Assets/LSG/manuals/ERCC92.zip). Trimmed reads were aligned to the Mus Musculus + ERCC STAR reference with STAR (version 2.7.11b) and alignment log files were compiled with MultiQC (version 1.26). Aligned reads were assessed for strandedness using RSeQC infer_experiment.py (version 5.0.4), gene body coverage using RSeQC geneBody_coverage.py (version 5.0.4), and distribution of RNA features using RSeQC read_distribution.py (version 5.0.4). Aligned reads from all samples were quantified using RSEM (version 1.3.3), with strandedness set to forward and RSEM count log files were compiled with MultiQC (version 1.26). To create a set of rRNA-removed quantification data, Ensembl IDs mapping to ribosomal RNA (rRNA) were removed from the RSEM gene count data. Both the original set of RSEM quantification data and the rRNA-removed data were subject to differential gene expression analysis as follows. A runsheet was generated with dp_tools (version 1.3.8) and the runsheet and quantification data were imported to R (version 4.4.2) with tximport (version 1.34.0), ERCC genes were removed, and the non-ERCC genes were normalized with DESeq2 (version 1.46.0) median of ratios method. Normalized gene counts were subject to differential expression analysis. Differential expression analysis was performed in R (version 4.4.2) using DESeq2 (version 1.46.0); all groups were compared pairwise using the Wald test and the likelihood ratio test was used to generate the F statistic p-value. Gene annotations were assigned using the custom annotation tables generated in-house as detailed in GL-DPPD-7110-A (https://github.com/nasa/GeneLab_Data_Processing/blob/GL_RefAnnotTable-A_1.1.0/GeneLab_Reference_Annotations/Pipeline_GL-DPPD-7110_Versions/GL-DPPD-7110-A/GL-DPPD-7110-A.md), with STRINGdb (version 2.16.4), PANTHER.db (version 1.0.12), and org.Mm.eg.db (version 3.19.1). Assessment of ERCC spiked genes was performed as detailed in the ERCC_analysis_GLbulkRNAseq.html report.
protocols.name: GeneLab RNAseq data processing protocol

protocols.description: Three hundred nanograms of total RNA were amplified and purified using Illumina TotalPrep RNA Amplification Kit (Ambion, Cat# IL1791) following kit instructions. Briefly, first strand cDNA was synthesized by incubating RNA with T7 oligo(dT) primer and reverse transcriptase mix at 42 C for 2 h. RNase H and DNA polymerase master mix were immediately added into the reaction mix following reverse transcription and were incubated for 2 hours at 16 C to synthesize second strand cDNA. RNA, primers, enzymes and salts that would inhibit in vitro transcription were removed through cDNA filter cartridges (part of the amplification kit). In vitro transcription was performed and biotinylated cRNA was synthesized by a 14 hour amplification with dNTP mix containing biotin-dUTP and T7 RNA polymerase. Amplified cRNA was subsequently purified and concentration was measured by NanoDrop ND-1000 Spectrophotometer (NanoDrop Technologies, DE). An aliquot of 750 nanograms of amplified products were loaded onto Illumina Sentrix Beadchip Array MouseRef8_V2 arrays, hybridized at 58 C in an Illumina Hybridization Oven (Illumina, Cat# 198361) for 17 hours, washed and incubated with streptavidin-Cy3 for 10 min to detect biotin-labeled cRNA on the arrays.
protocols.name: nucleic acid hybridization

protocols.description: Arrays were dried and scanned with a BeadArray Reader (Illumina, CA) and raw data were captured.
protocols.name: data collection

protocols.description: DNA Methylation and Reduced Representation Bisulfite Sequencing (RRBS) library construction. We processed 100 ng of isolated gDNA to generate RRBS DNA library using the Ovation RRBS Methyl-Seq System (NuGEN Technologies, #0353-32) according to the manufacturer's protocol. Briefly, the methylation insensitive MspI enzyme, which cuts the DNA at CCGG sites, was used to digest gDNA into fragments. The fragments were directly subjected to end blunting and phosphorylation in preparation for ligation to a methylated adapter with a single-base T overhang. A unique index, out of 96 indices, was used per sample for multiplexing. The ligation products were final repaired in a thermal cycler under the program (60 C for 10 min, 70 C for 10 min, hold at 4 C). The product of the final repair reaction was used for bisulfite conversion using kit QIAGEN EpiTect Fast DNA Bisulfite Kit according to Qiagen's protocol. Bisulfite-converted DNA was then amplified (Mastercycler pro, Eppendorf) and bead-purified with Agencourt RNAClean XP Beads.
protocols.name: DNA sequencing library construction
